name: CR-Int-11-linearity-3.f
questiontext:
Simplify and integrate \[\frac{{CT:0}}{{CT:1}}\] with respect to {{CT:2}}.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]
generalfeedback:
Using the distributive law and the properties of exponentials <hint>alg_indices</hint> we get that
\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \frac{{CT:0}}{{CT:1}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \frac{{CT:3}}{{CT:1}} - \frac{{CT:4}}{{CT:1}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:5}}
 \end{array}\]

So, using linearity in integration <hint>calc_int_linearity_rule</hint>,

\[\begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle
 \int \frac{{CT:0}}{{CT:1}} d{{CT:6}} &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int ({{CT:7}} - {{CT:8}}) d{{CT:6}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  \int {{CT:7}} d{{CT:6}} - \int {{CT:8}} d{{CT:6}} \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:9}} - {{CT:10}} + c \\
   &\displaystyle =&\displaystyle  {{CT:11}} + c
 \end{array}\]
